# Face Recognition & Tagging Requirements for RawDrive

> Terminology: See [`GLOSSARY.md`](GLOSSARY.md) (canonical terms for Workspace, Asset, Share Link, Trial, etc.).

## 1. Introduction & Scope

### 1.1. Purpose
This document outlines the requirements for a face recognition and tagging system within the RawDrive application. This feature will enable photographers to automatically detect, group, and identify people across their photo galleries, enhancing organization and searchability.

### 1.2. Scope
- The system will scan photos stored in the user's connected cloud storage (Google Drive/Dropbox).
- It will identify and group unique faces, allowing the photographer to assign names to them.
- It will create a new "People" view for browsing photos by person.
- The feature's visibility to end-clients will be configurable by the photographer on a per-gallery basis.

## 2. Core Architecture & Technical Requirements

### 2.1. Face Detection and Embedding
- The system shall use a high-accuracy, open-source deep learning model (e.g., FaceNet, Dlib) to perform face detection and generate high-dimensional vector embeddings for each detected face.
- This process will run as a non-blocking background job, initiated by the photographer. Progress will be communicated to the user via a UI element like the **ScanProgressToast**.

### 2.2. Vector Storage and Similarity Search
- The generated face embeddings shall be stored in the application's **PostgreSQL** database using the **`pgvector`** extension.
- When a new face is detected, its embedding will be compared against the existing embeddings in the database to find matches (i.e., other photos of the same person). This similarity search is the core of the grouping functionality.

### 2.3. Metadata Storage
- A new `People` table will be created to store information about identified individuals (e.g., Person ID, Name).
- A linking table will associate `Photos` with `People`, storing the location of the face tag on the image. This metadata-driven approach ensures the original image files are never modified.

### 2.4. Workflow Logic
- Face recognition will only be run on a photo if it has not been processed before.
- Once a photo is scanned, a flag will be set to prevent re-processing, unless a manual re-scan is initiated by the photographer.

## 3. User Experience (UX) & Application Components

### 3.1. For the Photographer (Admin)
- **Initiating Scan:** A new action will be available in the **AdminToolbar** or gallery view to "Scan for Faces" for one or more galleries.
- **People View (`PeopleView.tsx`):** A new top-level "People" route will be added to the main navigation. This view will display clusters of faces, grouped by presumed identity. Unnamed groups will be shown first.
- **Managing People (`PersonDetailView.tsx`):** From the People view, a photographer can:
    - Assign a name to a group of faces.
    - Merge multiple groups that represent the same person.
    - Remove incorrect photos from a person's group.
- **Manual Tagging (`FaceTagModal.tsx`):** In the **MediaViewer**, photographers should be able to manually draw a box around a face and tag it if the automated system missed it or identified it incorrectly.

### 3.2. For the Client
- **Opt-In Visibility:** The visibility of people tags to clients shall be disabled by default.
- **Gallery Setting (`GallerySettings.tsx`):** The photographer can enable a "Filter by Person" option in the gallery settings.
- **Filtering:** When enabled, clients will see a filter or search option in the gallery view that allows them to select a person's name and see all photos they appear in.

## 4. Privacy and Consent
- All face embedding data and people tags are strictly private to the photographer's account and will never be shared across different accounts.
- The feature is designed with photographer control in mind. No face information is shown to clients without the photographer's explicit action to enable it for a specific gallery.

## 5. Documentation
- The main `README.md` shall be updated with a note on the new feature and any significant system requirements (e.g., backend processing capabilities) needed to run the face recognition models efficiently.

# Face Recognition & Tagging Specification for RawDrive

## 1. Problem Statement

Photographers managing large photo galleries struggle to efficiently find and organize photos of specific people across their collections. Currently, there's no automated way to detect, group, and identify faces in uploaded photos, forcing photographers to manually tag individuals or rely on memory to locate specific photos.

## 2. User Story

**As a** professional photographer using RawDrive,
**I want** the system to automatically detect and group faces in my photos,
**So that** I can quickly find all photos of a specific person, assign names to them, and optionally allow my clients to filter photos by the people who appear in them.

## 3. Acceptance Criteria

### Happy Path Scenarios

**Scenario 1: Initiating Face Scan**
- **GIVEN** a photographer has photos in a gallery
- **WHEN** they click "Scan for Faces" from the gallery toolbar
- **THEN** a background job starts processing images, showing progress via ScanProgressToast

**Scenario 2: Viewing Detected Faces**
- **GIVEN** face scanning has completed for a gallery
- **WHEN** the photographer navigates to the "People" view
- **THEN** they see clusters of faces grouped by similarity, with unnamed groups shown first

**Scenario 3: Naming a Person**
- **GIVEN** the photographer is viewing a face cluster in the People view
- **WHEN** they assign a name to the cluster
- **THEN** all photos in that cluster are tagged with that person's name

**Scenario 4: Client Filtering (When Enabled)**
- **GIVEN** a photographer has enabled "Filter by Person" for a gallery
- **WHEN** a client views the gallery
- **THEN** they can filter photos by person name

### Edge Cases

**Scenario 5: No Faces Detected**
- **GIVEN** a gallery contains only landscape photos
- **WHEN** face scanning completes
- **THEN** the system shows "No faces detected" in the People view

**Scenario 6: Same Person in Multiple Clusters**
- **GIVEN** the system created separate clusters for the same person
- **WHEN** the photographer selects "Merge" on two clusters
- **THEN** all photos from both clusters are combined under one person

**Scenario 7: Manual Face Tagging**
- **GIVEN** the automated system missed a face
- **WHEN** the photographer draws a box around the face in MediaViewer
- **THEN** they can tag it with an existing or new person name

### Error Handling

**Scenario 8: Scan Failure**
- **GIVEN** a face scan is in progress
- **WHEN** processing fails for some images
- **THEN** the system logs errors, continues with remaining images, and reports partial completion

**Scenario 9: Invalid Image Format**
- **GIVEN** an unsupported image format is encountered
- **WHEN** the scanner processes it
- **THEN** it skips the image and logs a warning without stopping the entire scan

## 4. Technical Context

| Aspect | Value |
|--------|-------|
| **Affected Services** | backend, ai-processing-service, gallery-service, frontend |
| **Database** | PostgreSQL with pgvector extension |
| **AI/ML** | Face detection model (InsightFace/RetinaFace), face embedding extraction |
| **Dependencies** | pgvector, insightface, onnxruntime |
| **Constraints** | Background processing to avoid blocking UI, workspace isolation required |
| **Patterns to Follow** | Existing Celery worker pattern, Repository-Service-API architecture |

## 5. Non-Goals

- **Cross-workspace face matching** - Faces are strictly isolated per workspace
- **Real-time face detection during upload** - This is background processing only
- **Facial expression analysis** - Only identification, not emotion detection
- **External face recognition APIs** - Using local models only for privacy
- **Face data export** - No export of face embeddings or metadata
- **Client-side face tagging** - Only photographers can tag faces

## 6. Implementation Tasks

```tasks
## Phase 1: Database Schema & Models
- [ ] T001: Create Alembic migration for face recognition tables (faces, face_groups, face_assignments) | File: backend/migrations/versions/0185_face_recognition_tables.py
- [ ] T002: Create Face SQLAlchemy model with embedding vector field | File: backend/src/app/models/face.py
- [ ] T003: Create FaceGroup model for named person clusters | File: backend/src/app/models/face_group.py
- [ ] T004: Create FaceAssignment model linking faces to face_groups | File: backend/src/app/models/face_assignment.py
- [ ] T005: Add face_scan_status field to Asset model | File: backend/src/app/models/asset.py
- [ ] T006: Add show_people_filter field to Gallery model | File: backend/src/app/models/gallery.py

## Phase 2: AI Processing Service - Face Detection & Embedding
- [ ] T007: Add InsightFace model loader and face detection service | File: services/ai-processing-service/src/services/face_detection_service.py
- [ ] T008: Create face embedding extraction service | File: services/ai-processing-service/src/services/face_embedding_service.py
- [ ] T009: Create face detection API endpoint | File: services/ai-processing-service/src/api/v1/faces.py
- [ ] T010: Add face detection Celery worker task | File: services/ai-processing-service/src/workers/face_detection_worker.py

## Phase 3: Backend - Face Repository & Service Layer
- [ ] T011: Create FaceRepository for database operations | File: backend/src/app/repositories/face_repository.py
- [ ] T012: Create FaceGroupRepository for person cluster operations | File: backend/src/app/repositories/face_group_repository.py
- [ ] T013: Create FaceService with business logic for face operations | File: backend/src/app/services/face_service.py
- [ ] T014: Create FaceClusteringService for grouping similar faces | File: backend/src/app/services/face_clustering_service.py

## Phase 4: Backend - API Endpoints
- [ ] T015: Create faces API router with CRUD endpoints | File: backend/src/app/api/v1/faces.py
- [ ] T016: Create face_groups API router for person management | File: backend/src/app/api/v1/face_groups.py
- [ ] T017: Add scan trigger endpoint to galleries API | File: backend/src/app/api/v1/galleries.py
- [ ] T018: Register new routers in API v1 init | File: backend/src/app/api/v1/__init__.py

## Phase 5: Frontend - Types & Services
- [ ] T019: Create TypeScript types for face recognition feature | File: frontend/src/types/faces.ts
- [ ] T020: Create faceService for API communication | File: frontend/src/services/faceService.ts
- [ ] T021: Create useFaces hook for face data fetching | File: frontend/src/hooks/useFaces.ts
- [ ] T022: Create useFaceGroups hook for person cluster management | File: frontend/src/hooks/useFaceGroups.ts

## Phase 6: Frontend - People View Components
- [ ] T023: Create PeopleView page component | File: frontend/src/pages/workspace/PeopleView.tsx
- [ ] T024: Create FaceClusterCard component for displaying face groups | File: frontend/src/components/features/faces/FaceClusterCard.tsx
- [ ] T025: Create PersonDetailView for managing a person's photos | File: frontend/src/components/features/faces/PersonDetailView.tsx
- [ ] T026: Create FaceTagModal for manual face tagging | File: frontend/src/components/features/faces/FaceTagModal.tsx
- [ ] T027: Create ScanProgressToast component | File: frontend/src/components/features/faces/ScanProgressToast.tsx
- [ ] T028: Create MergeFacesModal for combining clusters | File: frontend/src/components/features/faces/MergeFacesModal.tsx

## Phase 7: Frontend - Integration
- [ ] T029: Add "Scan for Faces" button to gallery toolbar | File: frontend/src/components/features/gallery/GalleryToolbar.tsx
- [ ] T030: Add People filter to gallery view (for clients) | File: frontend/src/components/features/gallery/GalleryFilters.tsx
- [ ] T031: Add show_people_filter toggle to gallery settings | File: frontend/src/pages/workspace/GallerySettingsPage.tsx
- [ ] T032: Add People route to workspace routes | File: frontend/src/router/routes.tsx
- [ ] T033: Add People link to workspace sidebar navigation | File: frontend/src/components/layout/WorkspaceSidebar.tsx

## Phase 8: Testing & Documentation
- [ ] T034: Create unit tests for FaceService | File: backend/tests/unit/services/test_face_service.py
- [ ] T035: Create integration tests for faces API | File: backend/tests/integration/api/v1/test_faces.py
- [ ] T036: Create frontend component tests for PeopleView | File: frontend/tests/components/faces/PeopleView.test.tsx
- [ ] T037: Update feature documentation | File: docs/Features/face-recognition.md
```

## 7. Success Metrics

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Face detection accuracy | > 95% on clear frontal faces |
| Face clustering precision | > 90% same-person grouping |
| Scan throughput | > 10 images/second per worker |
| UI response time for People view | < 500ms for up to 1000 faces |
| Manual tag success rate | 100% save/retrieve reliability |

## 8. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| High compute cost for face embeddings | Use ONNX runtime for optimized inference, process in batches |
| False positives in face clustering | Configurable similarity threshold, easy merge/split UI |
| Large vector storage requirements | Use quantized embeddings (512-dim), periodic cleanup of orphaned data |
| Privacy concerns | Strict workspace isolation, no cross-tenant data access, clear documentation |
| Model size impact on deployment | Lazy model loading, shared model across workers |
